questions.question: Shippers package hazardous materials to ____ them.
questions.correctAnswerText: Contain
questions.explanation: Shippers package hazardous materials to keep them fully contained. Vehicles must display placards to show what cargo they are carrying.

questions.question: What should you do if a hazardous materials label will not fit on the package?

options.text: Place the label on a tag securely attached to the item.
Attach a QR Code to be scanned.
Reduce the size of the label to fit it on the item.

questions.correctAnswerText: Place the label on a tag securely attached to the item.
questions.explanation: If a hazard label will not fit on the package, attach it to a tag that is securely fastened to the package instead.

questions.question: What should you do before opening trailer doors during a fire?

options.text: Check to see if the doors are hot.
Find someone else to open the doors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check to see if the doors are hot.
questions.explanation: In a truck fire, feel the doors first to check if they are hot. If they are, there may be a cargo fire inside. Keep the doors closed because opening them could make the fire worse by giving it more oxygen.

questions.question: Which sign shows that your shipment may contain hazardous materials?

options.text: The shipper sells fireworks or munitions.
Your last shipment was labeled as hazardous.

questions.correctAnswerText: The shipper sells fireworks or munitions.
questions.explanation: A sign that a shipment may contain hazardous materials is when the shipper's business involves them. These include paint dealers, chemical suppliers, scientific suppliers, pest control, farms, and fireworks or explosives dealers.

questions.question: What should a driver do if given a leaking package of hazardous materials?

options.text: Leave it on the side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Refuse it.
questions.explanation: Drivers must refuse any leaking package or shipment of hazardous materials.

questions.question: Hazardous materials should be loaded:
questions.correctAnswerText: Away from heat sources.
questions.explanation: Always load hazardous materials away from heat sources. Some explosives and flammable materials cannot be loaded in cargo spaces that have heaters.

questions.question: What does a material's hazard class tell you?

options.text: The risks associated with the material.
How quickly the material must reach its destination.

questions.correctAnswerText: The risks associated with the material.
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials are placed into one of nine classes. Each class describes the type of risks that come with that material.

questions.question: When loading hazardous materials containers, you should not use:
questions.correctAnswerText: Hooks.
questions.explanation: Protect hazardous materials containers from damage. Never use equipment like hooks that could damage the containers or packaging.

questions.question: Which task is NOT your job as a driver at an accident scene?

options.text: Keeping people away from the scene.
Trying to put the fire out by yourself.
Telling emergency responders about the hazardous materials.

questions.correctAnswerText: Trying to put the fire out by yourself.
questions.explanation: At an accident scene, keep people away, limit spills if safe, and tell emergency responders about the hazardous materials. Do not try to fight the fire yourself unless you have the right equipment and training.

questions.question: What sign could show that cargo contains hazardous materials?

options.text: The cargo is in cylinder tanks.
The cargo is picked up from a supermarket.
The cargo is packaged on wood pallets.

questions.correctAnswerText: The cargo is in cylinder tanks.
questions.explanation: Cylinders and drums often hold hazardous materials. Take proper precautions when transporting cargo in these containers.

questions.question: What does a driver need to transport hazardous materials?

options.text: A CDL with a hazardous materials endorsement
A CDL with a tank endorsement
A CDL with a cargo endorsement

questions.correctAnswerText: A CDL with a hazardous materials endorsement
questions.explanation: To drive any vehicle carrying hazardous materials, you must have a CDL with a hazardous materials endorsement.

questions.question: What must a shipping paper list?

options.text: The location of fire departments along the planned route.

questions.correctAnswerText: An emergency response telephone number.
questions.explanation: Shipping papers for hazardous materials must include an emergency response telephone number.

questions.question: Who is responsible for labeling hazardous materials?
questions.correctAnswerText: The shipper
questions.explanation: The shipper is responsible for packaging, marking, and labeling hazardous materials. They must also provide warning placards.

questions.question: What shape are hazardous materials placards?
questions.correctAnswerText: A diamond
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials warning placards are diamond-shaped.

questions.question: Where must a hazardous materials placard be placed?

options.text: On the outside of the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: On the outside of the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials placards must be placed on the front, rear, and both sides of the vehicle.

questions.question: How must containers of hazardous materials be secured?

options.text: Braced to prevent movement during transportation.

questions.correctAnswerText: Braced to prevent movement during transportation.
questions.explanation: Containers must be braced so they do not fall, slide, or bounce during transportation.

questions.question: When loading compressed gas, should the liquid discharge valves be open or closed?
questions.correctAnswerText: Opened.
questions.explanation: Liquid discharge valves must be opened during loading and unloading, but closed at all other times.

questions.question: What should you do before opening trailer doors during a truck fire?

options.text: Check to see if the doors are hot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check to see if the doors are hot.
questions.explanation: Feel the doors first. If they are hot, there may be a cargo fire inside. Do not open hot doors.

questions.question: Is a shipping paper required for hazardous materials?

options.text: Only if kept in a digital file.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, for all shipments.
questions.explanation: Shipping papers are required for all hazardous materials shipments to communicate the risks of the materials.

questions.question: What should a driver check about shipping papers?

options.text: The shipping paper matches the markings and labels on packages.
The shipping paper is written in code.
All packages are labeled as poison.

questions.correctAnswerText: The shipping paper matches the markings and labels on packages.
questions.explanation: Compare the package markings and labels to the shipping papers. Make sure they match and the correct labels are on the packages.

questions.question: To choose the right placard, you need to know:

options.text: The hazard class of the materials.
The type of container holding the materials.

questions.correctAnswerText: The hazard class of the materials.
questions.explanation: To choose the right placards, you must know the hazard class of the materials, how much hazardous material you are shipping, and the total weight of all hazardous materials in your vehicle.

questions.question: ____ warn others about hazardous materials.
questions.correctAnswerText: Placards
questions.explanation: Diamond-shaped signs called placards are placed on packages and vehicles to warn drivers and others about hazardous materials. The shipper places the placards. The driver must check that the correct placards are in place.

questions.question: When carrying Division 1.1 explosives, you may park no closer than ____ from a building.
questions.correctAnswerText: 300 feet
questions.explanation: When carrying Division 1.1, 1.2, or 1.3 explosives, do not park within 300 feet of a bridge, tunnel, or building. The only exception is for short parking periods when you need to refuel or perform other necessary vehicle operations.

questions.question: When carrying Division 1.1, 1.2, or 1.3 explosives, your vehicle should not be:

options.text: Parked within 300 feet of a bridge.
Parked within 40 feet of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Parked within 300 feet of a bridge.
questions.explanation: Do not park a vehicle carrying Division 1.1, 1.2, or 1.3 explosives within 300 feet of a bridge, tunnel, or building, except briefly for necessary vehicle operations like refueling. Never park such a vehicle within five feet of the road.

questions.question: Hazardous materials placards are what shape?
questions.correctAnswerText: Diamond
questions.explanation: Vehicles carrying hazardous materials must display diamond-shaped warning signs on all four sides. These signs are called placards.

questions.question: When refueling a vehicle carrying hazardous materials:
questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off the engine.
questions.explanation: Turn off the engine before refueling a vehicle carrying hazardous materials. Someone must always stay at the nozzle and control the fuel flow while refueling.

questions.question: Hazardous materials placards are usually shaped like:
questions.correctAnswerText: Diamonds.
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials warning placards are diamond-shaped.

questions.question: Many products classed as poison are also:
questions.correctAnswerText: Flammable.
questions.explanation: Many hazardous materials that are poisonous are also flammable.

questions.question: An improperly placarded vehicle:

options.text: Can only be moved in an emergency.
Can be driven if the cargo is not radioactive.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can only be moved in an emergency.
questions.explanation: A vehicle that lacks proper placards for hazardous materials on board cannot be driven, except in an emergency to protect life and property.

questions.question: A placard should be placed:

options.text: At least three inches away from any other markings.
Under a ladder if space is limited.
On a background that is the same color as the placard.

questions.correctAnswerText: At least three inches away from any other markings.
questions.explanation: Place a placard at least three inches away from other markings. Keep it clear of attachments like doors and ladders. Always place placards against a background of a contrasting color.
